summary: Backend-only retest of the ADMIN_EMAILS digest dedupe fix (iter29 follow-up). RESULT: FIX CONFIRMED — 11/11 assertions pass across 2 test files. (a) db.admin_email_digests has unique index key_1 {'key':1, unique:true} present after backend startup (no manual creation in the test). (b) Run 1 emailed jenn@sailmorenow.com exactly once and created exactly 1 claim doc. (c) Run 2 immediately after did NOT re-email and the collection still held exactly 1 doc for that key (previous duplicate-upsert bug gone). (d) Run 3 after backdating sent_at 9 days re-emailed exactly once and refreshed the SAME doc's sent_at (still 1 doc). (e) Per-recipient fault isolation verified by injecting a Mongo failure (RuntimeError from update_one/insert_one) for one of two ADMIN_EMAILS addresses: the failing address was skipped while the healthy address (jenn@) was still claimed + emailed. Additionally validated the server.py _startup duplicate-collapse migration: dropped key_1, seeded 2 legacy docs with the same key, restarted backend -> only the doc with the latest sent_at survived and the unique index was recreated. All test data cleaned up (admin_email_digests empty, admin users' admin_report_digest_sent_at restored, ADMIN_EMAILS env restored).

minor.issue: Case mismatch between the two dedupe paths: `extra` comes from admin_emails() (lowercased) but the skip check is `extra in target_emails` where target_emails holds the raw u['email']. If an admin user's stored email has any uppercase, the same person is emailed twice (once via the users path, once via the admin_email_digests path). Suggest comparing lowercased values.

When a fresh (in-window) claim doc exists, matched_count==0 so the code always attempts an insert_one that is guaranteed to raise DuplicateKeyError. Works, but produces an avoidable write + Mongo duplicate-key error every run. A find_one/{key} short-circuit would be cleaner.

Two user documents exist with the same email jenn@sailmorenow.com and platform_role='admin'. The digest de-dupes because target_emails is a set, but duplicate admin user records are a data-integrity smell (users has a unique index on user_id only, not email).

action_items: Optional polish only: lowercase-normalize the `extra in target_emails` comparison in scheduler.py so an admin whose stored email has uppercase does not get two digests.
Optional: avoid the guaranteed DuplicateKeyError write when a fresh claim doc already exists.
critical_code_review_comments: scheduler.py:317-332 — claim logic is now correct and idempotent: non-upsert stale refresh (modified_count==1 => send) followed by a guarded insert_one relying on the unique index. Verified with real Mongo.

server.py:137-156 — duplicate collapse runs before create_index and is idempotent; verified by seeding legacy duplicates and restarting. Note it is O(dupe keys) with a second find per key, acceptable at this scale.
scheduler.py:314-335 — per-recipient try/except now isolates failures; verified that a raising recipient does not abort the remaining recipients.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter29_admin_digest_dedupe.py runs the digest job 4x with mailer.send_email monkeypatched; IMPORTANT: it keeps admin USERS' admin_report_digest_sent_at fresh so the ADMIN_EMAILS/admin_email_digests branch is the one exercised (backdating user stamps makes the users path win and the digest doc is never touched — that caused a false failure earlier). test_iter30_startup_collapse.py drops key_1, seeds duplicates and restarts backend via supervisorctl (~15s). pytest.ini forces xdist loadscope, so keep all assertions sharing a fixture in one class.
rca_of_the_issue: iter29 bug (upsert with a freshness predicate in the filter re-inserting a duplicate doc and re-sending) is resolved: uniqueness is now enforced at the DB level (unique index on admin_email_digests.key created at startup after collapsing legacy duplicates) and the claim is insert-first/non-upsert-update, so a filter miss now means 'already claimed' instead of 'insert again'. Per-recipient try/except prevents a single Mongo error from dropping the remaining recipients.
